proof.result: clippy exit 0. artifacts_concurrency ok. 10 passed: all nine row-named tests plus the rework test. Full suite 196 passed, 0 failed across 16 targets (180 before). A REAL DEFECT WAS REPRODUCED AND FIXED. The witness passed and code review returned SHIP, yet the mandatory FLOW-01 adversarial review still reproduced a permanent per-reference denial of service with an executed probe: a panic inside transfer() unwound past both the outcome send and finish(), so the watch channel never closed (every Waiter keeps the shared slot's sender alive) and the slot was never removed from inflight. Every present and future request for that reference hung forever, slot stuck RUNNING with neither CAS called. Bounded correctly: permit and temp reservation ARE released as locals dropped during unwind, so it leaked a slot only, never wrong or unverified bytes. FIX: a Resolution guard built before transfer(). The normal path calls answer(), which sends and sets its flag synchronously; Drop then only removes the slot. Any other exit makes Drop send Failed(Aborted) first, then remove. Chosen over catch_unwind because it also covers the task being dropped in place. The panic is NOT swallowed: unwinding still reaches the task boundary so tokio reports it, plus an ERROR log. The implementer also closed a hazard its own fix introduced, that Drop takes the inflight lock so a panic under it would poison the mutex and break every future download for every reference, worse than the original defect; all five lock sites now use table(), recovering via into_inner(). New test a_panic_in_the_transfer_task_does_not_wedge_the_reference, shown failing first.
